text:
Daria Ionescu, Senior Game Systems Architect at Nexu Interactive, based in Bengaluru, India. Email: daria.ionescu@nexuinteractive.com | Phone: +91 9876543210 | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/dariaionescu | GitHub: github.com/dariaionescu. With a decade of expertise in game systems architecture, I specialize in crafting scalable, high-performance solutions across Unity and Unreal Engine. My work has driven cross-team collaboration, optimized rendering pipelines, and reduced latency in multiplayer networks by 35% at Stellar Interactive.  

Over the past eight years, I’ve evolved from a Game Development Intern at Lumina Studios to a Senior Game Systems Architect at Nexu Interactive, leading teams of 8–12 developers. At Vortex Games, I designed reusable Unity systems that cut asset loading times by 22%, enabling faster iteration on a AAA title. At Stellar Interactive, I spearheaded the transition from Unity to Unreal Engine for a flagship project, refining physics simulations and integrating Vulkan for real-time rendering. My role at Nexu Interactive now encompasses architecting core systems for a live-service game, mentoring junior engineers, and collaborating with QA and design to align technical constraints with creative vision.  

Technical expertise spans Unity and Unreal Engine, where I’ve architected core systems, optimized memory usage, and implemented cross-platform solutions. In Unity, I developed a modular networking framework that supported 500+ concurrent players, while in Unreal, I optimized particle systems to reduce CPU overhead by 18%. My work with 3D graphics includes leveraging OpenGL for post-processing effects in a mobile title and Vulkan for multi-threaded rendering in a PC game. C# and .NET underpin much of my Unity work, while Python scripts automate build pipelines and asset management. Game physics simulations, such as implementing ragdoll mechanics in Unreal, have been central to several projects. Networking systems, including latency compensation and object replication, have been a focus since my early days at Vortex Games.  

Bachelor of Science in Computer Science from Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, 2015. Graduated with a focus on real-time systems and graphics programming, which directly informed my later work in game development.  

Fluent in English and Romanian, with intermediate proficiency in Hindi. My bilingual capabilities have facilitated communication with international teams and local stakeholders.  

Certifications include Unity Certified Developer (2020), Unreal Engine Advanced Certification (2022), and a Game Physics Specialization from Coursera. These credentials underscore my commitment to mastering both foundational and cutting-edge techniques in game systems design.
